item.title: NASA set to roll Artemis rocket back for urgent repairs after yet another delay
item.description: NASA is about to roll its Artemis II moon rocket back to the Vehicle Assembly Building to fix a helium flow issue that guarantees astronauts won't fly around the moon in March.

item.title: 2,800-year-old mass grave of women and children discovered in Serbia reveals 'brutal, deliberate and efficient' violence
item.description: An analysis of a mass grave found in northern Serbia is revealing new information about violence in Early Iron Age Europe.

item.title: Incomplete remains of world's 'youngest' impact crater spotted lurking in Chinese forest — Earth from space
item.description: A 2021 satellite photo shows off the recently uncovered Yilan crater in China, which is most likely the youngest impact structure on Earth. The incomplete ring is also the largest of its kind and only the second impact crater ever found in the country.

item.title: How to see the March 3 'blood moon' eclipse from anywhere on Earth
item.description: The final "blood moon" total lunar eclipse until 2029 is coming to North America this Tuesday (March 3). Here's how to watch it online.

item.title: Coros Pace 4 smartwatch review: A capable and affordable fitness tracker
item.description: The Coros Pace 4 packs lots of features into a small and light fitness tracker. It's not perfect, but it could make the ideal first serious smartwatch for workouts.

item.title: Obesity is linked to 1 in 10 deaths from infection worldwide — and scientists are still learning why
item.description: A new study finds that people with obesity are more likely to be hospitalized with or die from severe infections.

item.title: Far fewer people are related to Genghis Khan than previously assumed, new genomic study suggests
item.description: Some experts have suggested as many as 1 in 200 men in the world are related to Genghis Khan. But a new genomic study reveals the number is significantly lower.

item.title: 14,000-year-old ivory tools found in Alaska hint at how Clovis ancestors first arrived in the New World
item.description: Ancient artifacts unearthed in Alaska revealed migrants from Asia might have come to the Americas via an inland route, and not a coastal path.

item.title: Scientists find genetic 'switch' in mice that turns caring dads into violent brutes
item.description: A new study suggests that the Agouti gene in the brains of male African striped mice can act as a molecular "switch," making them caring or violent toward their young.

item.title: James Webb telescope spots giant auroras rolling through Uranus' atmosphere
item.description: JWST observed Uranus for nearly a full rotation, charting the planet's upper atmosphere and magnetic environment for the first time.
